So, explain how the OPSEC works for those who don't know or have clue.

OPSEC is just short for OPerations/OPerational SECurity.

It's simply the process of identifying and analyzing your threat model and engineering countermeasures to make your operation/self more secure.

In this case, I'm referring to your privacy and anonymity when browsing the web.

If you're asking what you should be doing for OPSEC, at a minimum harden your firefox install (or use TOR Browser), run linux, use a VPN, segregate all of your activities, don't use the same username across websites, etc, anything that could give away your identity.

There's a fuckton to do and to learn about this and I won't get into it all here, but if you're interested and have specific questions, I can answer them no problem. I just don't want to write a huge novel on OPSEC.

The example here of clicking on tracking links would obviously be a big nono in regards to maintaining your privacy online.

So, to not do that:

For example this is a clean link: https://twitter.com/TheDrunkJake/status/1108215723514572800

This is a link with trackers.

https://twitter.com/TheDrunkJake/status/1108215723514572800?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw%7Ctwcamp%5Etweetembed&ref_url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.buzzfeed.com%2Fryanschocket2%2F18-tweets-from-this-week-that-are-straight-up-comedy-gold

They both take you to the same place. As you can see everything beyond the string "?ref" is completely unnecessary and is strictly used for tracking. Most websites use this format. Anything with a "?" is typically a red flag (it's a reserved or 'unsafe' character), as URLs don't have "?" in them. It's a character to let the browser know that the URL has finished and to pass on the parameters afterwards in a query. Anything after the "?" is not relevant to where the link takes you.

Unless disabled, any webpage with the facebook, twitter, instagram "share" buttons, is tracking you. Even if you don't interact with them (ie click on them).

There's a lot to learn to really increase your anonymity on the web.
